text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Federal government provided money in 1996 budget for take-off of six newly created states, national planning minister Ayo Ogunlade says in southwestern Ondo state.
- Government scraps ceiling on interest rates, says finance minister Anthony Ani at meeting of World Bank in Washington.
- Lagos state suspends 2.7 billion naira road contracts as it begins rehabilitation of 100 roads through direct labour.
- Customs department says five senior officers dismissed and several others retired in bid to sanitise the service.
- Finance minister Anthony Ani tells World Bank and International Monetary Fund in Washington that Nigerian pump prices will be determined by a proposed energy commission.
- Secretary of opposition NADECO group Ayo Opadokun said to have been freed from detention but family says unaware of this.
- Nigeria welcomes decision of Commonwealth to resume dialogue over nation's suspension from the group.
- Exiled Nigerian Nobel laureate Wole Soyinka in a Voice of America radio programme criticises Britain and United States for allegedly "abetting" continued military rule in Nigeria.
- Nigerian stock exchange suspends trading in shares of Coca-cola bottlers Nigerian Bottling Company over its plan to merge with another soft drinkers maker Sapanda Industries Ltd.
- Code of ethics for bankers to be released soon, says Chartered Institute of Bankers of Nigeria.
